recentItems.title: How AI disinformation is reshaping our reality | Myriam Francois | TEDxCambridge University
recentItems.description:
We are reaching a point where distinguishing fact from fiction is becoming increasingly difficult. Dr. Myriam François argues that the rise of highly convincing AI-generated disinformation is unfolding alongside growing pressures on journalism and the institutions responsible for verifying and communicating facts.

As journalists face increasing threats and a small number of technology companies play a greater role in shaping how information is distributed, personalised algorithms can use our digital behaviour to influence what we see, believe, and engage with. This raises an important question: what happens when societies can no longer agree on a shared baseline of facts?

Without that common foundation, independent thought, public trust, and democratic participation can become increasingly fragile. Protecting the integrity of our information ecosystem is therefore not simply a challenge for journalists or technology companies, but a broader responsibility for all of us. Dr. François is an award-winning journalist, filmmaker, and writer, and an alumna of Newnham College Cambridge, as well as Georgetown and Oxford University where she completed her PhD in 2017. She’s a former presenter of The Stream on Al jazeera and currently presents her own show The Tea on YouTube. She has worked extensively across the BBC, Channel 4, and other international outlets. Her directorial debut documentary Finding Alaa as Bafta and Academy award Longlisted and has received multiple international awards, and her writing has appeared in publications including The Guardian, TIME, and Foreign Policy. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Adaptation: Our greatest undoing? | Sulaiman Adewale | TEDxOsogbo
recentItems.description: What would banking look like with no interface at all, just a conversation in whatever language you already speak? This talk argues that our biggest risk isn't outdated technology; it's how comfortable we get with things that merely work. It challenges us to stop managing what's broken and start fixing it. Sulaiman Adewale is the founder of Xara, Africa's first AI-powered conversational banking assistant, built entirely inside WhatsApp. A self-taught software engineer from Osogbo, Osun State, he spent over a decade in software architecture before building Xara out of personal frustration: he found that even simple banking tasks meant fighting an interface that wasn't built for him. Rather than adapt to broken systems the way most of us quietly learn to, he asked what banking would look like with no interface at all, just a conversation, in whatever language a user already speaks, from Pidgin to Yoruba to Hausa. Launched in 2025, Xara now serves over sixty thousand users and has drawn interest from major financial and technology players, including xAI. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: AI Is Learning. But About Africa? | Francis Odeyemi | TEDxOsogbo
recentItems.description: How much of Africa actually exists in the datasets shaping today's AI? This talk makes the case that data is power, and that if Africa doesn't teach AI who it is, someone else will, with consequences for whether the continent is even part of the future conversation. Francis Odeyemi is a product and brand design leader and the founder of Ninthgrid, often called the "Shutterstock for Africa," a platform giving African photographers a way to earn from authentic, Afrocentric imagery while supplying brands with visual content that actually reflects the continent. Over more than a decade, he has built digital products across Nigeria, the UK, and the US, and is a Y Combinator Startup School alumnus with executive education from Stanford's Graduate School of Business. Through Ninthgrid, he has watched firsthand what happens when an AI model is asked to picture Africa, and how little of the continent actually exists in the datasets shaping today's AI. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The World's Favorite Advice: "Follow Your Passion" | Segun Solomon | TEDxOsogbo
recentItems.description: "Follow your passion" is the most repeated advice young people receive. This talk challenges it, arguing that passion is fuel, not a destination: competence carries you, purpose gives you somewhere to go, and direction gets you there. It walks through the missing first step most people skip, and the real equation of value, scale, and trust behind sustainable success. Segun Solomon is the founder and CEO of Madros Technologies, where he leads IT consulting, digital skills development, and brand innovation across Nigeria. He also founded Tech Parrot, a technology media platform, and built the Madros Academy of Technologies into a training ground for thousands of young people entering the digital economy. Beyond his companies, Segun shapes policy as a member of the Technical Working Group under Nigeria's National Information Technology Development Agency and serves on the Osun State Advisory Board on Technology, Innovation, and Digital Economy. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Day I Stopped Waiting | Kemi Deborah Olakunle | TEDxOsogbo
recentItems.description: This talk is about the moment of deciding to stop waiting (for permission, for the right conditions, for someone else to act) and start building the solutions you want to see. It's a decision that has already reshaped how thousands of women access care. Kemi Deborah Olakunle, known widely as Kemi the Changemaker, is a social entrepreneur with a background in Human Anatomy and advanced training in Public Health. She founded HealthVest, a health-tech venture whose flagship product, PreggiCare Wallet, helps women save toward pregnancy and childbirth while accessing discounted care. PreggiCare Wallet is one piece of her broader push for a Nigeria where quality healthcare isn't a privilege. She also leads the Art4Health Campaign and founded Changemakers Hub and Capital, which has trained and mentored over two thousand young people across multiple countries. Through the Solve Africa Fund, she's working to raise a million changemakers across Africa. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: You are public health | Oluwatomi Olunuga | TEDxOsogbo
recentItems.description: Public health isn't something that only happens in hospitals and ministries. This talk argues that it's built or broken in the everyday choices we make for ourselves and each other, and that everyone is already a public health actor, whether they have realized it or not. Oluwatomi Olunuga is a public health and development professional with over nine years of experience advancing health, gender equality, and the rights of women and girls across Nigeria and beyond. She is the founder of Careers in Public Health, which has supported over 3,400 students and professionals through mentorship and career development, and of the MaleMatters Initiative, which engages men and boys as partners in gender equity. Her work with organizations including UNFPA, Women Deliver, and GSMA, alongside her current role at Helium Health, has earned her recognitions including the Diana Award and a place on She Leads Africa's Top 50 Rising Moguls list. recentItems.title: How much can we ignore? | Manuela Alaedin | TEDxEscola Concept Ribeirão Preto
recentItems.description: Can cruelty become so familiar that we stop recognizing it as cruelty? In this talk, the speaker shares the story of her family's adoption of a cat that had been a victim of abuse. This experience led her to reflect on how repeated exposure to cruelty can make us less sensitive to suffering and even cause us to accept it as normal. The talk invites us to question what we have become accustomed to, recognize the suffering of others, and remember that something does not become acceptable simply because we see it happen too often. recentItems.title: What does it mean to be intelligent? | Alice Macedo | TEDxEscola Concept Ribeirão Preto
recentItems.description: Does struggling with math mean you are not intelligent? In this talk, the speaker reflects on a personal experience that sparked a deeper question about how we define intelligence and why academic grades often receive more recognition than creativity, artistic expression, and other talents. Drawing on Howard Gardner's theory of multiple intelligences, the talk challenges traditional ideas of academic success and explores how schools and society can better recognize different abilities. It invites us to rethink what it truly means to be intelligent and how education can prepare us for life beyond the classroom. recentItems.title: Can a machine make me more creative? | Laura Francelin | TEDxEscola Concept Ribeirão Preto
recentItems.description: Can artificial intelligence kill creativity, or can it help more people express their ideas? In this talk, the speaker shares how AI helped turn song lyrics into a complete song for a school talent show, despite not yet knowing how to play a musical instrument. Combining this personal experience with research on AI in education and examples of using AI as a creative partner, the talk explores the opportunities and risks of these tools. It challenges us to consider how AI can support, rather than replace, human imagination and creativity. recentItems.title: Why your brain can't beat an algorithm | Cauã Oliveira | TEDxEscola Concept Ribeirão Preto
recentItems.description: Have you ever planned to watch short videos for just 15 minutes, only to realize that an entire hour has passed? In this talk, the speaker explores how social media algorithms use our brain's reward system and dopamine to keep us scrolling longer than we intend. By examining the psychology behind these platforms, the talk reveals why self-control alone can be difficult and offers practical strategies to regain control of our attention and develop healthier digital habits. recentItems.description: What makes an extraordinary experience truly meaningful? In this talk, the speaker reflects on a trip to Disney World that brought unexpected feelings of homesickness and a deeper appreciation for family. Combining personal storytelling, interviews with peers, and research on happiness and human relationships, the talk explores how the people we love shape our dreams, memories, and most meaningful experiences. It invites us to look beyond the experiences we chase and recognize the importance of sharing them with others. recentItems.title: You're changing (even if you don't see it) | Alice Zanardi | TEDxEscola Concept Ribeirão Preto
recentItems.description: Why is it easier to notice how other people change than to recognize how we change ourselves? In this talk, the speaker reflects on reconnecting with an Australian friend after years apart and realizing that both of them had changed in ways they had not fully noticed. Connecting this personal experience to psychological research on bias, the talk explores how our perceptions of others and ourselves can differ, reminding us that personal growth often happens quietly, one small change at a time.
